transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Hello, doctor. I've been feeling deeply depressed and sad for the past two months. I just can't seem to shake this heavy mood, and it's been going on almost every day.
Have you ever had a period of time when your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or you felt unusually energetic or impulsive?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. Lately, and really for most of my life, I've just felt very down and depressed. I definitely haven't had any times where I felt unusually energetic or high.
When you say you've felt down for most of your life, how long exactly have you been experiencing this low mood?

While I've had my usual ups and downs over the years, this really severe and constant low mood has been going on specifically for the last two months. Before this, I had some bad days, but it was never this persistent or heavy.
Did anything stressful or significant happen around the time your mood started worsening two months ago?

I honestly can't think of any specific event or trigger that happened back then. Nothing major or particularly stressful occurred in my life around that time. This heavy mood just seemed to start on its own.
Before these last two months, would you say you had a low mood that lasted for more than two years on and off?
No, I don't think I've had a low mood lasting that long before this. I'm not really sure, as my main struggles have really just been over these past two months.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Major Depressive Disorder", "Persistent Depressive Disorder"], but Persistent Depressive Disorder is now ruled out because the patient denies having a low mood lasting for more than two years prior to the current episode. The current episode is severe and persistent but only began two months ago without a history of chronic depressive symptoms, which makes Major Depressive Disorder the most appropriate diagnosis. No manic or hypomanic symptoms were reported, and no specific stressor was identified, supporting the diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder without specifiers like 'with psychotic features' or 'with seasonal pattern'.
